description: Curated cross-reactivity groups, consumed alongside any drug-reference source (json, atc or ddinter). ATC classification cannot express cross-branch pharmacological cross-reactivity — aspirin (N02BA01, salicylates) and ibuprofen (M01AE01, propionic-acid derivatives) sit in different ATC branches yet share the NSAID hypersensitivity family — so that linkage is carried here as data (the boundary documented in ADR Decision 24, closed by this file). A group links every drug whose ATC code falls under any of its atcPrefixes; the safety validator warns when a checked drug shares a group with a recorded allergy (cross-reactivity) or with an active order (additive / duplicate-class therapy), and the injector treats group-related active orders as relevant to a drug-specific question. Seed data — expand per deployment.

groups.name: NSAID
groups.note: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: hypersensitivity commonly cross-reacts across chemically distinct NSAID branches, including salicylates
groups.rationale: The COX-1-inhibiting NSAID branches - butylpyrazolidines (M01AA), acetic acids such as diclofenac and indometacin (M01AB), oxicams (M01AC), propionic acids such as ibuprofen and naproxen (M01AE), fenamates (M01AG), salicylates (N02BA) and pyrazolones such as metamizole (N02BB) - because cross-reactive NSAID hypersensitivity follows COX-1 inhibition across chemical families. Left out: the selective COX-2 inhibitors (M01AH), the alternative such patients are usually given; M01AX, which mixes in non-NSAIDs; and paracetamol (N02BE). ADR Decision 195. The COX-2 inhibitors are still NSAIDs beside another, so they join for the screen's duplicate-therapy summary only (duplicateTherapyAtcPrefixes) - never for an allergy's cross-reactivity, nor a proposal's class relationship. ADR Decision 197.

groups.name: Penicillins
groups.note: Penicillins: an allergy to one penicillin is treated as an allergy to every penicillin
groups.rationale: Every penicillin shares the beta-lactam-thiazolidine nucleus most penicillin allergy is raised against, and standard guidance treats a recorded allergy to one penicillin as an allergy to them all. ATC files them in four subgroups, so no shared subgroup relates them: extended-spectrum penicillins such as amoxicillin and ampicillin (J01CA), beta-lactamase-sensitive penicillins such as benzylpenicillin and phenoxymethylpenicillin (J01CE), beta-lactamase-resistant penicillins such as cloxacillin and flucloxacillin (J01CF), and penicillins combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor such as amoxicillin-clavulanate (J01CR). Left out: the beta-lactamase inhibitors alone (J01CG), which are not penicillins, and the cephalosporins and carbapenems, whose cross-reactivity with a penicillin allergy is low and which such patients are often given. ADR Decision 229.
